statement.p: A graph of the velocity function v(t) of an object moving in a straight line is given above. Velocity is measured in m/s, and time in seconds.

a) What is the object's maximum velocity?
?
s
m/s
m

b) What is the object's maximum displacement?
?
s
m/s
m

static.solution:
Solution:
a) The maximum velocity is the highest value on the graph, v = 3 m/s.
b) Since v \geq 0 on [0, 13], the maximum displacement is the entire area under the curve on this interval. Break up the integral into rectangles and triangles. \int_{0}^{13} v(t) \, dt = \int_{0}^{2} v(t) \, dt + \int_{2}^{5} v(t) \, dt + \int_{5}^{9} v(t) \, dt + \int_{9}^{13} v(t) \, dt = (2)(3) + \frac{1}{2}(3)(3) + \frac{1}{2}(4)(3) + (4)(3) = 28.5 The units are m (meters) because displacement is a distance measurement.
